article.headline: Storm Boelo Triggers 80mph Winds Across Scotland Following Destructive Storm Austen
article.summary: An amber weather warning is in place for Scotland, Northern Ireland, and northern England as Storm Boelo brings potential travel chaos and power cuts this weekend.
article.body:
Gusts reaching up to 80mph are expected to lash exposed coastal areas as Storm Boelo arrives just one day after Storm Austen caused widespread destruction. While the National Grid managed to restore power to over 60,000 properties following Friday's winds, more than 10,000 homes remained in the dark Friday evening as emergency teams prepare for a second bout of extreme weather. In Brighton, the structural integrity of the iconic 1866 West Pier failed under the pressure of the previous storm, resulting in a section collapsing directly into the sea.

Residents across much of Scotland, northern England, and parts of Northern Ireland face significant disruption as the storm sweeps through. The severe weather threatens to topple trees, damage buildings, and trigger further power outages. Beyond the immediate risk of structural damage, the combination of heavy rain and high winds creates hazardous conditions for commuters, with authorities cautioning that flying debris could pose a danger to life throughout the weekend.

The Met Office has issued an amber weather warning effective from 21:00 Saturday until 21:00 Sunday, noting the unusual length of the alert over such a wide geographical area. ScotRail has confirmed cancellations for some train services, and Network Rail is implementing speed restrictions across large parts of Scotland. Police Scotland have urged drivers to avoid unnecessary journeys as officials coordinate through the government's resilience room.

Conditions are expected to remain volatile through Sunday, with the strongest winds initially impacting the west before moving eastwards. Meteorological reports indicate that winds will begin to ease gradually from the west as the system passes through the region by Sunday evening.

article.headline: Julio Enciso strikes to hold Nottingham Forest in 1-1 Premier League draw
article.summary: Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest shared the points at Portman Road after Julio Enciso neutralized Neco Williams’ opening goal.
article.body:
Nottingham Forest finished the match with 17 shots compared to Ipswich's seven, yet managed only a single goal from 2.31 worth of expected goals. Forest have now scored just six times from 13.4 worth of chances created, marking the team as the biggest underperformer in expected goals data this season. The result leaves Forest with only one win from their opening eight games.

This draw highlights a recurring theme for Ipswich Town, who have now secured seven points from losing positions this season, more than any other team in the Premier League. The point earned at Portman Road matches the total points Ipswich achieved during their entire 2024-25 campaign in the competition.

Neco Williams opened the scoring for Forest before a mistake from Nikola Milenkovic allowed Julio Enciso to equalize just before halftime. The match featured significant VAR controversy, as referee Thomas Bramall reviewed a challenge by Ipswich defender Issa Diop on James McAtee. Despite being sent to the pitchside monitor, Bramall opted to issue only a yellow card, ruling that Diop did not deny an obvious goal-scoring opportunity. Forest manager Oliver Glasner expressed frustration with the decision, calling it a clear red card. 

Late-game action saw Leif Davis clearing the ball off the line twice for Ipswich. Meanwhile, Liam Delap and Callum Hudson-Odoi both struggled to convert, and Forest suffered a setback when Neco Williams exited the match with an arm injury late in the second half. The draw keeps both sides searching for consistency as the league season progresses.

article.headline: Delta Goodrem returns to Strictly Come Dancing floor after fractured rib recovery
article.summary: Australian singer Delta Goodrem is set to perform on Saturday after missing one week of the BBC competition due to a rib injury.
article.body:
Delta Goodrem captured the emotional toll of her recovery in an Instagram post, sharing hospital clips that documented her progress over the past two weeks. The 41-year-old singer described the experience of being sidelined by a fractured rib as gutting, noting that she had to learn to appreciate small steps while remaining patient during her absence from the ballroom. In her message to fans, she declared that she is back to fight, telling those facing their own battles that she sees them and remains with them as a fighter.

Her return is critical for her continued participation in the competition. BBC rules stipulate that contestants are permitted to skip only a single week of the show before they are required to withdraw. With her health now cleared by medical professionals, Goodrem is set to rejoin professional dancer Kai Widdrington to perform a rumba to Celine Dion's “It's All Coming Back To Me Now” during the upcoming live show.

Goodrem missed last week's performance, which was known as Icons Week. During her absence, Widdrington stepped in to dance with fellow professional Amy Dowden in a tribute to the late musical legend Dolly Parton. The BBC officially confirmed on Monday that the singer had been given the all-clear to dance again this coming weekend. The return of the pair, affectionately dubbed Team DeltaKai by fans, will see all 12 remaining contestants on the floor for week five of the current series. The program will continue its broadcast schedule this Saturday night as the competition moves forward following the mandatory week-long rest period.

For the Bucks, the priority is addressing the defensive vulnerabilities that led to back-to-back high-scoring losses, while the 76ers look to maintain their winning momentum in front of a home crowd at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

According to Yahoo Sports, the Bucks are coming off a quick turnaround following their Friday night loss. The 76ers have navigated their early schedule with Tyrese Maxey leading the backcourt and Joel Embiid anchoring the frontcourt. However, roster management is a key factor for Philadelphia; as reported by NBC Sports Philadelphia, LeBron James is listed as questionable for the game due to low back and sciatica management. Dean Wade is also questionable with an ankle injury, while teammates Dominick Barlow, Tacko Fall, and Ariel Hukporti remain out.

Looking ahead, Joel Embiid has indicated he will sit out one game of the team's current back-to-back schedule, meaning he is expected to miss either this clash with Milwaukee or the subsequent game against the Detroit Pistons on Sunday. The team will determine his availability based on their internal load management plan.

Charlotte continues its rebuilding phase following the offseason trade of LaMelo Ball, while the Hornets have listed Christian Anderson as probable for Saturday’s game due to an ankle injury. Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., and Nick Richards debuted for their respective squads this week, with Thompson struggling on Friday to find rhythm from beyond the arc. article.headline: NC State fires Dave Doeren following 31-28 loss to Stanford
article.summary: NC State dismissed head football coach Dave Doeren on Saturday after 14 seasons following a loss to Stanford.
article.body:
The 54-year-old coach compiled a record of 98-74 during his time with the Wolfpack, finishing his tenure as the winningest coach in program history. His departure arrives less than 24 hours after a 31-28 defeat at Stanford, a game in which the Wolfpack trailed early by 14-0 and never held the lead. NC State currently sits at 3-4 overall and 1-3 in conference play.

This decision carries significant financial weight for the university. Under the terms of his contract, which was scheduled to run through December 31, 2029, the school could owe Doeren approximately $9.75 million in remaining base salary. The change in leadership follows a season that failed to meet expectations, starting with a blowout loss at Virginia and a defeat at Vanderbilt, despite initial hopes of competing for an ACC championship.

Athletics director Boo Corrigan announced the firing on Saturday, noting his appreciation for the leadership and passion Doeren brought to the role over 14 years. While rumors regarding Doeren's future had circulated previously, the coach had stated he was not considering retirement. The team's performance has struggled throughout the month, including a 38-14 home loss to Wake Forest earlier in October.

Running backs coach and special teams coordinator Todd Goebbel will assume head coaching duties for the remainder of the season. NC State still has five games remaining on its schedule, including home matchups against California, Duke, and Syracuse, before concluding the season against Florida State and UNC. Meanwhile, the university has officially initiated a national search to find a permanent replacement for the head coaching position.

article.headline: India snatches four-wicket T20 victory over Black Caps in Christchurch thriller
article.summary: India defeated the Black Caps by four wickets at Hagley Oval to take a 2-0 lead in the five-match T20 series.
article.body:
Tilak Varma hammered 51 not out off just 26 balls to secure the win, anchoring an unbeaten 69-run partnership for the seventh wicket with Nitish Kumar Reddy that saw India reach their target with only a ball to spare. This result marked the second time in two matches that the Black Caps suffered a loss in the final over, leaving them to face a desperate fight in the remainder of the series to avoid defeat. 

For the Black Caps, the result comes despite a dominant bowling display from captain Mitchell Santner, who returned figures of 4-21. Santner’s spell at Hagley Oval had reduced India to 112-6 in the 15th over, appearing to put the home side in a position of control while defending a total of 180-5. Earlier, Glenn Phillips hit 70 off 43 balls and Bevon Jacobs added 58 off 46 to stabilize the innings after the top order collapsed to 41-3 within the power play. 

According to the NZ Herald, the momentum shifted when the New Zealand bowling attack was hampered by the unavailability of Matt Henry and a fielding penalty imposed during the final over. Varma capitalized on these conditions, hitting six boundaries and one six to dismantle the Kiwi attack. 

The two sides are now set to travel to Wellington for the third game of the series. The Black Caps must win the remaining three matches to secure a series victory.

article.summary: Oklahoma faces Mississippi State in a Week 8 matchup at 3:30 p.m. ET, bolstered by the return of key offensive linemen.
article.body: Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is available to start today after being left off the final injury report, anchoring a Bulldogs offense that averages 32.5 points per game. The team will also wear special helmet stickers today to support offensive lineman Sean Hutton, who remains hospitalized in stable condition following a rare medical event on Wednesday. Mississippi State’s passing attack, led by Taylor’s 17 touchdowns, will be tested against an Oklahoma defense that has allowed only 18.1 points per game and recorded 18 sacks this year. Oklahoma aims to reach a .500 record and gain momentum as they navigate a difficult conference schedule. The game kicks off at Davis Wade Stadium at 3:30 p.m. ET, with coverage available on the SEC Network.

For the Red Bulls, the stakes of this fixture are immense. Michael Bradley’s team faces significant pressure after suffering three defeats in their last five matches, including consecutive losses against Toronto FC and DC United. The club now faces the difficult challenge of overcoming one of the conference’s most consistent teams to improve their standing in the final stretch of the season.

Inter Miami, managed by Kily Gonzalez, looks to overcome the deficit in the second half of the match. While the team remains in a secure position in the conference standings, the current scoreline forces an adjustment from the visiting squad to avoid an upset against a desperate New York side. All eyes remain on the second half to see if the league's top-performing side can secure a comeback victory or if New York will solidify their path toward a playoff spot.

Hundreds of injuries and arrests have been reported amid a violent police crackdown, along with widespread damage to public and private property. The student demands are an outgrowth of the “Flamingo Revolution,” which erupted earlier this year in opposition to a luxury resort being developed on the ecologically sensitive Sazan Island.
